Repository: django/django
Base commit: bebd4cfa8f5e0d2dff2de5e50d86e849a40f4bb2
### Issue
prefetch_related_objects() does not work for reused model instances.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Dennis Kliban)
	 
Our project processes instances in a stream. In some cases the instances are repeated. In these cases, we discovered that prefetch_related_objects() does not set the to_attr on all of the instances if the first instance in the list already has it set.
When Django determines that the very first instance in the list is_fetched[0], it does not call into the the prefetch_one_level()[1]. The attributed specified in the to_attr parameter is only set in the prefetch_one_level() method[2].
is_fetched is set by looking for the to_attr attribute on the instance[3].
[0] ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/stable/2.2.x/django/db/models/query.py#L1605-L1609
[1] ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/stable/2.2.x/django/db/models/query.py#L1624
[2] ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/stable/2.2.x/django/db/models/query.py#L1799
[3] ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/stable/2.2.x/django/db/models/query.py#L1708

### Candidate patch
```diff
diff --git a/reproduce_prefetch_issue.py b/reproduce_prefetch_issue.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..e7e2d9b6e0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/reproduce_prefetch_issue.py
@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+import django
+from django.conf import settings
+from django.db import models
+from django.db.models.query import prefetch_related_objects
+
+settings.configure(
+    INSTALLED_APPS=[
+        '__main__',  # This allows us to include our models in the script
+    ],
+    DATABASES={
+        'default': {
+            'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.sqlite3',
+            'NAME': ':memory:',
+        }
+    }
+)
+
+django.setup()
+
+from django.db import connection
+
+# Manually create the model tables
+from django.db.migrations.operations.models import CreateModel
+from django.db.migrations.state import ProjectState
+
+state = ProjectState()
+CreateModel(
+    name='RelatedModel',
+    fields=[
+        ('id', models.AutoField(primary_key=True)),
+        ('name', models.CharField(max_length=100)),
+    ]
+).state_forwards(app_label='__main__', state=state)
+
+CreateModel(
+    name='MainModel',
+    fields=[
+        ('id', models.AutoField(primary_key=True)),
+        ('related', models.ForeignKey('RelatedModel', on_delete=models.CASCADE)),
+    ]
+).state_forwards(app_label='__main__', state=state)
+
+# Apply the state changes to the database
+state.apps.ready = True
+for model in state.apps.get_models():
+    model._meta.managed = True
+    model._meta.db_table = model._meta.label_lower
+    with connection.schema_editor() as schema_editor:
+        schema_editor.create_model(model)
+
+# Define a simple model for demonstration purposes
+class RelatedModel(models.Model):
+    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
+
+class MainModel(models.Model):
+    related = models.ForeignKey(RelatedModel, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
+
+# The database tables are now created, and we can proceed with creating instances
+
+# Create instances of RelatedModel
+related_instance1 = RelatedModel.objects.create(name='Related 1')
+related_instance2 = RelatedModel.objects.create(name='Related 2')
+
+
+# Create a stream of model instances
+instances = [
+    MainModel.objects.create(id=1, related=related_instance1),
+    MainModel.objects.create(id=1, related=related_instance1),
+    MainModel.objects.create(id=2, related=related_instance2)
+]
+
+# Create a Prefetch object with the to_attr parameter
+prefetch = models.Prefetch('related', to_attr='custom_related')
+
+# Attempt to use prefetch_related_objects with Prefetch object
+prefetch_related_objects(instances, prefetch)
+
+# Check if to_attr is set on all instances
+for instance in instances:
+    print(hasattr(instance, 'custom_related'), getattr(instance, 'custom_related', None))
+
+print("Script completed successfully, no errors.")

```

parsed.reason: The patch introduces a new test file that is not part of the original codebase and does not address the issue described. It also lacks context and explanation, making it difficult to understand its purpose and impact.
